title: Just One Thing
format: Authored held-pose animatic; not full animation

panels.description: An empty wall hook. One framed flower rests directly below it. He notices the picture.
Insert: the flower picture waiting on the floor.
Insert: the empty hook above it.
He approaches with an easy smile.
He bends and takes the left edge of the frame.
He lifts the picture. This should be easy.
Almost at the hook, he notices a slight tilt.
He pauses, thinking. Perhaps he should measure first.
A ruler appears in his hand. He is delighted with this sensible preparation.
He carefully measures the existing hook.
He adjusts the ruler by a tiny amount.
Now he checks the ruler with a spirit level.
Close: the bubble is already in the middle.
He lowers his tools and looks pleased. The picture is still on the floor.
He reaches for the picture again, then stops to remember something.
Another idea. He needs a checklist.
He sets up a desk on the other side of the room.
He writes a short list with careful concentration.
Insert: three preparation steps checked; the flower task remains empty.
He admires his progress.
Wide: the picture has not moved.
He looks at the picture, then back at his list.
He writes a second list to improve the first.
A third revision.
Then another. Preparation is growing.
He raises his perfect checklist. It unrolls almost to the floor.
He peers around the long list, still trying to look satisfied.
He needs a way to organize all of this.
A large planning board takes its place between him and the task.
First, the flower card: the original goal.
He adds a card for the measuring step.
Then the tools.
Then how to choose the tools.
Then how to organize the choosing.
The board is full. He draws connections everywhere.
Close: the route from the flower card is now a tangle.
He proudly unveils his system. The little picture still waits.
He starts following the connections with his finger.
The route takes him back to the same card.
He consults the checklist again.
The checklist points him back to the board.
He checks the ruler again.
Then checks the checklist again.
His eyes droop. He is tired, but nothing is done.
The clock has marched on.
Wide: a room full of preparation. The picture is still in exactly the same place.
He sits back against the desk, drained.
His eyes find the flower picture across the room.
Insert: warm light on the small, uncomplicated picture.
He looks up to the hook. The task has never changed.
He looks at the tangled board one last time.
He sets the pencil down. No new plan.
He stands and turns toward the picture.
He walks away from the desk.
Past the board, toward the task.
He stops at the picture.
He bends and grips the frame.
He lifts it.
He places the wire over the hook.
He lets go. It stays there.
He steps back to admire it.
The picture is slightly crooked.
His eyes flick back toward the ruler and planning board.
He almost reaches for the old solution.
Then he smiles, turns and nudges the frame with one hand.
He drops his hand. That was all it needed.
He walks away from the finished picture, leaving the elaborate system behind.
Final image: one picture on the wall; a huge planning apparatus for a tiny completed task.
